result.title: Disentangling Where and When:Factored Spatio-Temporal Explanations for Video Action Recognition
result.comment: Accepted at The Fortieth Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
result.summary: Post-hoc explanation methods for video action recognition typically conflate spatial appearance and temporal dynamics into a single saliency or importance map. We propose a perturbation-based framework that disentangles these contributions into a spatial appearance mask ($M_a$) and a temporal motion mask ($M_m$). The two masks are jointly optimized against a frozen action recognition model through factored perturbation architecture, with nearest frame replacement to identify important temporal dynamics. A separation penalty discourages the appearance mask from spending budget on frames that the motion mask has already discarded. A ReLU-based area constraint penalizes explanations larger than an assigned budget. To evaluate these explanations, we introduce a separation protocol that sweeps spatial pixels and temporal frames independently, backed by proofs characterizing the proposed method. Across EPIC-Kitchens-55, EGTEA Gaze+, and Something-Something V2, our method attains the lowest deletion AUC against leading baselines while producing masks roughly five times sparser.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出基于扰动的视频动作识别后验解释框架，将证据拆成空间外观掩码与时间运动掩码，在冻结模型上联合优化并加入分离惩罚与面积约束，同时设计分别扫描像素与帧的评估协议。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把外观与运动证据分离并用扰动与删除曲线衡量各自因果贡献的表述与评价方式，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选和空间、时间贡献归因提供可供核查的思路，但对象是视频动作识别而非多模态推理状态。
